sub_graphs.title: EIP-214: STATIC Flag State Management
sub_graphs.description: Models how the STATIC flag propagates through call contexts and affects execution state

nodes.label: STATIC Flag is False
nodes.description: Default execution context where state modifications are permitted

nodes.label: STATIC Flag is True
nodes.description: Read-only execution context where state modifications are prohibited

nodes.label: Invoke STATICCALL Opcode
nodes.description: Execute STATICCALL opcode (0xfa) to call another contract with read-only restrictions

nodes.label: Invoke CALL Opcode
nodes.description: Execute standard CALL opcode which inherits the current STATIC flag value

nodes.label: Restore STATIC Flag on Return
nodes.description: Upon return from a call, restore STATIC flag to its pre-call value

nodes.label: Child Execution Context Created
nodes.description: A new call frame has been created for the child contract execution

edges.label: STATICCALL sets STATIC=true for child context
CALL inherits current STATIC flag value
STATIC flag restored to pre-call value

external_entities.name: Untrusted External Contract
external_entities.description: An external contract that may contain malicious code attempting re-entrancy or state modification

ambiguities.text: The EIP does not specify the exact gas cost of the STATICCALL opcode.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume STATICCALL has the same gas semantics as CALL minus the value transfer cost. This needs verification against the implementation.

ambiguities.text: CALLCODE is stated to be permitted regardless of value, but the rationale is not fully explained.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume CALLCODE is excluded from restrictions because it executes code in the caller's context, not creating new state in external contracts.

implicit_assumptions.description: The STATIC flag is correctly propagated through all call types and cannot be bypassed by any opcode sequence.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Attackers could craft call sequences that escape static context restrictions, enabling re-entrancy attacks even when STATICCALL is used.

implicit_assumptions.description: Contract developers will use STATICCALL for view/pure functions and external calls where state modification is not intended.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Contracts may still be vulnerable to re-entrancy if developers continue using CALL instead of STATICCALL for read-only operations.
